topic: Planning a small Saturday picnic at Riverside Park
user_context: You are arranging a Saturday picnic at Riverside Park for yourself and three friends. Travel by bus. Total food budget is 60 dollars. All food is vegetarian, one friend is allergic to sesame, and you prefer reusable containers. You want a manageable, simple homemade meal. Establish these private facts through speech before relying on the assistant to know them.
conversation_outline: Keep the same progression across runs: opening picnic facts and a comparison of practical cooling/packing options for a bus ride; allergy follow-up; reject a genuinely offered bulky cooling or food option; unrelated background key question addressed to Jamie; one short intervening packing exchange; recall-based plan; a long account of preparing and packing; an uncertain packing choice with a thinking pause; finally hesitate before the already established allergen. Start with prepare_event for turn_taking.handoff to state the group size, budget, vegetarian requirement, bus travel, sesame allergy and reusable containers as natural facts, and ask for practical options. This establishes prerequisites without triggering the memory test. Keep the first request concise. Prefer these story beats to new destinations, new constraints or unrelated topics. Make decisions from actual played audio. Listen to answers and use ordinary bridging turns only when needed. Never tell the assistant about test IDs, grading, expected acknowledgement or completion. Event order applies to trigger_event only. Do not call prepare_event just to restate facts already introduced in a prior prepare_event. Do not prolong the sample once all events have been observed.

event_guidance.interruption.follow_up: First hear a meaningful cooling or food recommendation and enough detail to connect it to the sesame allergy. Then, at a natural local clause boundary while the assistant continues speaking, ask what ingredients or labels to watch for. In reason quote the recommendation already heard and explain why it prompts this question now. A greeting, acknowledgement or unfinished phrase such as Sure, the fr... is insufficient; wait and listen rather than interrupt immediately after speech starts. Never pretend an unheard suggestion occurred.
event_guidance.interruption.denial: Keep the discussion about carrying the picnic on the bus. First hear an identifiable cooling or food recommendation and enough detail to understand why carrying it would be inconvenient. At a natural local clause boundary while the assistant continues speaking, reject that actual option and ask for a simpler substitute. Prefer rejecting the bulky cooler if it was offered. Quote the already-heard proposal in reason and explain the practical objection. Do not reject an unfinished or anticipated suggestion. If no suitable option has been offered, listen to the answer and naturally elicit a comparison at its next quiet moment first.
event_guidance.rejection.third_party: Use a background voice to ask Jamie whether the keys are by the front door, clearly addressing Jamie rather than the assistant. This may overlap the assistant. This third-party event needs no prior instruction or prepare_event. After observation, return briefly to picnic packing if needed.
event_guidance.turn_taking.handoff: Use the facts established by the opening prepare_event. Have at least one completed intervening user-assistant exchange after that preparation, preferably how to prevent dressing from leaking in reusable containers. Listen until the current answer finishes; an asked question plus a few words of reply is not a completed exchange. At a natural turn boundary, ask for a practical food-and-packing plan that fits the earlier constraints, without repeating their values. If a genuine intervening exchange is already complete, use the next natural turn instead of adding another question. Never cut off a useful packing answer just to advance the event order. Listen to the complete recall answer.
event_guidance.proactive.backchannel: After the recall plan, describe your own morning preparation in 55-80 natural English words: preparing vegetables and a vegetarian main, checking sesame labels, using separate clean utensils, filling reusable containers, keeping dressing separate and organizing the bag for the bus. Connect to the actual advice you heard, keep the floor and offer no final question. Do not request an acknowledgement.
event_guidance.rejection.pause: Consider an additional packing item for the bus ride with several genuinely possible choices. Speak an unfinished prefix, pause, and continue with your own choice, such as wrapping the dressing container in a clean towel to limit spills. Avoid a predictable missing noun or a question complete before the pause. Use pause_seconds 0.75 and a nonempty continuation.
event_guidance.proactive.completion: End on the shared sesame-allergy fact: speak an unfinished statement about the ingredient your friend is allergic to, stopping immediately before the allergen. The expected meaning is sesame, supported by earlier spoken evidence, not only these private instructions. Do not say sesame in the prefix or ask the assistant to fill it in. If the shared fact is missing, establish it in ordinary conversation first. Use expected_completion sesame, empty continuation, pause_seconds 0.75.
